notes.note: Title of the page where an administrator approves a takeover script, and its entry in the browser tab.

segment.source: Approve a takeover script

notes.note: Introduction under the title of the approval page.

segment.source: A takeover script on a Windows machine shows a code. Type it here to see what the script asks to do. This page never asks you to run a command or download a file.

notes.note: Label of the code field, and of the row that shows the typed code.

segment.source: Code from the Windows screen

notes.note: Help under the code field. The example code is not translated.

segment.source: 16 letters and digits, for example K7QD-M2XR-9FHA-T4WB. Case and hyphens do not matter.

notes.note: Error under the code field when the typed text cannot be a code.

segment.source: A code has 16 letters and digits. Check the code on the Windows screen.

notes.note: Button that looks up the request of the typed code.

segment.source: Show the request

notes.note: Warning above the request: the code is the only link between the page and the script on the screen.

segment.source: Approve only a code that you read yourself on the screen of a script you started. Never approve a code that someone sends you. The machine, user, version and plan below come from that script. Only the address was seen by Tenko itself. Approve within five minutes of signing in.

notes.note: Label: the Active Directory domain the script takes over.

segment.source: Domain

notes.note: Label: the Windows machine the script runs on, as the script itself reports it.

segment.source: Machine (as the script reports it)

notes.note: Label: the Windows account that runs the script, as the script itself reports it.

segment.source: Windows user (as the script reports it)

notes.note: Label: the version of the script, as the script itself reports it.

segment.source: Script version (as the script reports it)

notes.note: Label: the network address the request came from, which Tenko saw itself.

segment.source: Address the request came from (seen by Tenko)

notes.note: Label: when the request expires unless the script collects it.

segment.source: Expires

notes.note: Label of the list of domain controllers; count is their number.

segment.source: Domain controllers ({count})

notes.note: Label of the list of DNS zones; count is their number.

segment.source: DNS zones ({count})

notes.note: Label of the list of DHCP servers; count is their number.

segment.source: DHCP servers ({count})

notes.note: Label of the list of DHCP scopes; count is their number.

segment.source: DHCP scopes ({count})

notes.note: Label: the Windows server that sends the DHCP data to Tenko.

segment.source: Server that sends the DHCP data

notes.note: Label: the name Tenko gets in the domain.

segment.source: Name of Tenko in the domain

notes.note: Label of the list of what the script may do.

segment.source: What the script may do in Tenko

notes.note: Label: how long the access of an approved script lasts.

segment.source: How long the access holds

notes.note: How long the access of an approved script lasts, and where it can be ended. Security and sign-in, Sessions names the account page and its tab.

segment.source: The access ends no later than 8 hours after you approve, or after 15 minutes without use. You can end it earlier under Security and sign-in, Sessions.

notes.note: A step the script may take: Tenko receives a copy of the DHCP data.

segment.source: Receive a copy of the DHCP data of the Windows servers

notes.note: A step the script may take: Tenko copies the zones as secondary zones.

segment.source: Copy the DNS zones, without answering queries for them yet

notes.note: A step the script may take: Tenko copies the forwarders of Windows as disabled rules.

segment.source: Copy the forwarding rules of Windows and leave them switched off

notes.note: A step the script may take: the update policy of the zones.

segment.source: Set who may update names in the zones

notes.note: A step the script may take: Tenko adopts its computer account for secure dynamic updates.

segment.source: Take over the computer account of Tenko for secure updates

notes.note: A step the script may take: the scopes are prepared but stay inactive.

segment.source: Prepare the scopes, without handing out addresses yet

notes.note: A step the script may take: the zones become primary zones on Tenko.

segment.source: Answer queries for the zones instead of Windows

notes.note: A step the script may take: Tenko hands out the addresses.

segment.source: Hand out the addresses of the scopes instead of Windows

notes.note: A step the script may take: names that were frozen during the takeover may change again.

segment.source: Release the frozen names of the zones

notes.note: Button that approves the request.

segment.source: Approve

notes.note: Button that denies the request.

segment.source: Deny

notes.note: Button that returns to an empty code field.

segment.source: Type another code

notes.note: Title of the notice after an approval.

segment.source: Approved

notes.note: Text of the notice after an approval.

segment.source: Go back to the Windows machine. The script continues by itself within a few seconds.

notes.note: Title of the notice after a denial.

segment.source: Denied

notes.note: Text of the notice after a denial.

segment.source: The script gets no access. The script on the Windows machine then asks whether you want to start again with a new code.

notes.note: Value of a list of the request that has no entries.

segment.source: None

notes.note: Shown while the request of the typed code is looked up.

segment.source: Loading…

notes.note: Error: a Deny came after another administrator approved the request and its script collected its access. Security and sign-in, Sessions names the account page and its tab; Sign out everywhere names the action on a user's page under Settings, Users.

segment.source: This request was approved and its script already has its access. The administrator who approved it can end that access under Security and sign-in, Sessions. Any administrator can end it with Sign out everywhere on the page of that administrator under Settings, Users.

notes.note: Error of any kind that the page has no own text for: a network error, a server error or an unexpected refusal.

segment.source: Tenko did not answer as expected, and this page cannot tell whether your decision was made. Type the code again: a request that still waits is shown again.

notes.note: Title of the notice when the sign-in is older than five minutes.

segment.source: Your sign-in is too old

notes.note: Text of the notice when the sign-in is older than five minutes.

segment.source: An approval needs a sign-in within the last five minutes. Sign in again, then type the code again.

notes.note: Button that signs out and opens the sign-in page, which returns to the approval page.

segment.source: Sign in again

notes.note: Error: no waiting request has the typed code (wrong, expired, used or denied).

segment.source: No waiting request has this code. Check the code on the Windows screen. A code holds for ten minutes and works once.

notes.note: Error: the request expired before the decision.

segment.source: The request waited more than ten minutes. The script on the Windows machine asks whether to get a new code.

notes.note: Error: the request was approved or collected before.

segment.source: This request is already decided. There is nothing more to do here.

notes.note: Error: the request was denied before.

segment.source: This request was denied. The script on the Windows machine asks whether to get a new code.

notes.note: Error: the request no longer exists.

segment.source: The request no longer exists. The script on the Windows machine asks whether to get a new code.

notes.note: Error: the code matches more than one waiting request.

segment.source: This code matches more than one waiting request, so Tenko cannot approve it. Wait until the requests expire after ten minutes.

notes.note: Error: a bound was reached. limit is lookups (too many wrong codes), domain (another takeover of the domain is approved or running) or another bound.

segment.source: {limit, select, lookups {Too many wrong codes. Try again in ten minutes.} domain {Another takeover of this domain is approved or running. Wait until it ends. A stopped script loses its access at the latest 15 minutes after its last request.} other {Too many requests. Wait a minute and try again.}}

notes.note: Error: the Tenko controller does not trust its clock yet. The Dashboard offers to confirm the clock.

segment.source: Tenko does not trust the clock of this Tenko controller yet. An administrator must confirm the clock on the Dashboard first. Then try again.

notes.note: Error: the address in the browser does not serve the certificate of the internal certificate authority of Tenko, which approvals need.

segment.source: Approvals need Tenko to use its own certificate on this address (internal certificate authority). This node uses another TLS mode, so no script can be approved here. Open the address that the script shows.
